scenes.headline: Old Plex servers are being hacked
scenes.body: The bug chain is called Plex2Shell
scenes.say: Run Plex at home? Hackers are breaking into old Plex servers.

scenes.headline: Four flaws, one chain
scenes.body: Together they can let an attacker run code on your server.
scenes.say: Plex2Shell is four flaws in Plex Media Server. Chained together, the researcher says, they let an attacker run code on your server.

scenes.headline: Exploited in the wild
scenes.body: CISA added all four to its list of exploited bugs.
scenes.say: On October twentieth, the US agency CISA listed all four as exploited in real attacks.

scenes.headline: NAS owners report break-ins
scenes.body: QNAP says some customers' Plex servers appear compromised.
scenes.say: On November sixth, QNAP said some customers' Plex servers appear compromised.

scenes.headline: Crypto miners and proxy software
scenes.body: Updating alone won't remove what they installed.
scenes.say: Hacked servers have run crypto miners and proxy software, and updating alone won't remove them.

scenes.headline: Your media server is a computer too.
scenes.say: Analyst note: a media server is still a computer on your home network, so patch it like one.

scenes.headline: Do this tonight
items: Turn off Remote Access if unused
scenes.say: Tonight: update Plex to the latest version, turn off Remote Access if you don't use it, and if an old version was open online, reset your passwords.

scenes.headline: The security story behind the headline.
scenes.say: Sources are in the description. Follow Securidge.
